## PCR Primer Design Rules

| Parameter | Target |
|---|---|
| Length | 18–25 nt |
| GC content | 40–60% |
| Tm | 55–65 °C |
| Tm difference between primers | ≤ 2–5 °C |
| GC clamp | 1–2 G/C in the last 5 bases at the 3′ end; no more than 3 |
| Runs | ≤ 4 of a single base; ≤ 4 dinucleotide repeats |
| Self-complementarity | Hairpin ΔG > −3 kcal/mol (3′ end), > −6 (internal) |
| Primer-dimer | Self-/cross-dimer ΔG > −5 kcal/mol (3′ end), > −6 (internal) |
| 3′ end | No T as the final base if possible; avoid 3′ mismatches |
| Specificity | BLAST against the template genome; unique binding site |
| Amplicon size | 100–1000 bp (standard); 70–200 bp (qPCR) |

### Tm Estimation

```text
Wallace rule (< 14 nt):      Tm = 2(A+T) + 4(G+C)
Basic (> 13 nt):             Tm = 64.9 + 41 × (G+C − 16.4) / N
Salt-adjusted:               Tm = 81.5 + 16.6·log10[Na+] + 0.41(%GC) − 675/N
Nearest-neighbor:            most accurate; use for real design
```

### Annealing Temperature

```text
Ta = Tm(lowest primer) − 3 to 5 °C
Optimal Ta = 0.3 × Tm(primer) + 0.7 × Tm(product) − 14.9
```

### Standard Reaction (50 µL)

| Component | Final concentration |
|---|---|
| Buffer | 1× |
| MgCl₂ | 1.5–2.5 mM |
| dNTPs | 200 µM each |
| Forward primer | 0.1–0.5 µM |
| Reverse primer | 0.1–0.5 µM |
| Template DNA | 1–10 ng plasmid; 10–100 ng genomic |
| Taq polymerase | 1–2.5 U |
| Nuclease-free water | to 50 µL |

### Thermocycling

```text
Initial denaturation   95 °C   2–3 min          1×
Denaturation           95 °C   15–30 s     ┐
Annealing              Ta      15–30 s     ├  25–35×
Extension              72 °C   1 min/kb    ┘  (Taq); 15–30 s/kb (Phusion/Q5)
Final extension        72 °C   5–10 min         1×
Hold                   4 °C    ∞
```

### qPCR-Specific

| Parameter | Target |
|---|---|
| Amplicon | 70–200 bp |
| Probe Tm | 5–10 °C above primer Tm |
| Probe 5′ end | No G (quenches FAM) |
| Efficiency | 90–110% (slope −3.1 to −3.6) |
| R² of standard curve | ≥ 0.98 |
| Span exon–exon junction | For cDNA; avoids gDNA amplification |

### Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| No product | Lower Ta, raise Mg²⁺, check template/primers, add cycles |
| Non-specific bands | Raise Ta, touchdown PCR, lower Mg²⁺, reduce primer/template |
| Primer-dimers | Redesign primers, lower primer conc., hot-start polymerase |
| Smear | Less template, fewer cycles, shorter extension |
| GC-rich template | Add 3–10% DMSO or 1 M betaine; use GC buffer |

### Contamination Control

- Physically separate pre-PCR and post-PCR areas
- Unidirectional workflow: reagent prep → template addition → amplification → analysis
- Dedicated pipettes and filter tips
- Always include a no-template control (NTC); add no-RT control for RT-PCR
- Aliquot reagents; use UNG/dUTP carryover prevention when needed
